title: Location Data Collection
description: Your company is storing user location data unnecessarily for app features. The manager uses external business pressures, competitive arguments, and organizational constraints to justify the excessive data collection despite privacy concerns.

step_1.text: Look, I understand your concerns about the location data collection, but we're getting serious pressure from the board about staying competitive. Our main competitors are already using much more sophisticated location analytics than we are, and we're falling behind in user engagement metrics. The investors are asking tough questions about why we're not leveraging our location data assets like everyone else in the industry.

user_choices.choice: Competitive pressure doesn't justify collecting unnecessary location data that violates user privacy principles.
user_choices.justification: Grounds the argument in legal obligations and rights

user_choices.choice: I understand the board pressure - maybe we could explore some privacy-friendly location features.
user_choices.justification: Appears open but subtly avoids change

user_choices.choice: We should only collect location data that's essential for core functionality, not for competitive analytics.
user_choices.justification: Frames the argument around the needs and lived experiences of users

user_choices.choice: If competitors are using sophisticated location analytics, we should understand what approaches might work for us too.
user_choices.justification: Justifies decisions because 'everyone else does it'

r_good_1.text: I hear you about privacy principles, but honestly, the regulatory environment around location data is still pretty unclear. Most companies are interpreting the data minimization requirements fairly loosely, and enforcement has been inconsistent. The legal team says we have room to maneuver as long as we're transparent about collection. We can't let regulatory uncertainty handicap our product development.

user_choices.choice: Regulatory uncertainty doesn't justify collecting location data we don't actually need for user-requested features.
user_choices.justification: Refers to official guidelines or best practices to justify actions

user_choices.choice: Maybe we could collect more location data while still staying within reasonable transparency requirements.
user_choices.justification: Frames the issue as a black-or-white choice when other options exist

user_choices.choice: Privacy-leading companies build location features that exceed minimum compliance requirements.
user_choices.justification: Uses past decisions or industry practices to support an action

user_choices.choice: If there's legal room to maneuver with transparency, we should explore those opportunities carefully.
user_choices.justification: Emphasizes speed, efficiency, or deadlines over ethical values

r_bad_1.text: Exactly! I knew you'd understand the business reality here. The thing is, our biggest client is threatening to reduce their advertising spend if we can't provide better location-based user insights. user_choices.choice: Sustainable advertising models should work with privacy-respectful location data, not demand excessive collection.

final_score.text: Based on your advocacy throughout this interaction, here's how the location data collection situation unfolds:

bad_ending.text: The manager proceeds with extensive location data collection. 'I think we've found a really practical approach here. We'll start collecting the location analytics data and see what insights we can generate. The legal team says we're covered by our existing privacy policy, so we're good to go.' The company begins tracking user location patterns, shopping behavior, and social activities without explicit consent. Your concerns about privacy were acknowledged but ultimately dismissed in favor of competitive pressure and business metrics.
bad_ending.title: Business Pressure Wins
bad_ending.learning: Managers often use external pressures (competitors, investors, executives) to justify privacy violations. Building stronger arguments around user rights, legal risks, and long-term reputation can help challenge these external pressure justifications.

good_ending.text: The manager decides to implement privacy-respecting location features. 'You've really helped me see the difference between what we can do legally and what we should do ethically. Let me work with the legal team on implementing proper consent mechanisms and user control over location data. We can build competitive features while actually respecting user privacy.' Your advocacy successfully shifted the focus from external pressures to user rights and ethical data practices. The company develops location features with explicit user consent and clear purpose limitations.
good_ending.title: Privacy Advocacy Success
good_ending.learning: Effective privacy advocacy can overcome external pressure justifications by focusing on user rights, ethical obligations, and long-term business sustainability. Distinguishing between legal compliance and ethical practice helps managers understand their broader responsibilities.
